newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, seen under pressure.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, seen under pressure.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Friday in line with losses in the underlying cash market where rumours about the financial stability of a Japanese construction company pulled down Tokyo stocks.
The firm, Tobishima Corp, denied the rumours but the Nikkei share average lost 171.39 points to close at 17,867.04.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract on SIMEX ended 185 points lower at 17,840 after hitting an early high of 18,300.
Dealers said interest was slow and volumes thin with many local traders out for the Chinese New Year holiday.

"People were trying to lock in profits from the morning rise," said a trader with a Japanese futures house. He added that further gains were also stifled by continued worries about the financial sector and caution ahead of a meeting of finance ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations.
"Technically, there's also quite a lot of resistance above the 18,400 level. My gut feeling is it's going lower," he said.
A close below the key 17,800 support level would expose the March Nikkei to further declines, he said.
Dealers said the dollar's rally towards 124 yen was not affecting the Nikkei as most market players were expecting it to reach 125 yen in the near future.
"Up to 125 yen is already priced in. The Nikkei won't respond much to that," said the trader.
